title: Folding an Operator Over a List with oplist and apply
description: Pass an operator procedure as a first-class parameter to fold a list recursively and compare it with built-in apply.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `oplist` takes two parameters: a binary procedure `op` and a non-empty list `L`. Lines 3-4 check the single-element base case: when `(null? (cdr L))` is true, `L` has only one item left and `oplist` returns `(car L)`.
When `L` has more than one element, line 5 calls `(op (car L) (oplist op (cdr L)))`. This combines the front element `(car L)` with the result of folding `op` over `(cdr L)`.
Notice how `op` on line 2 is a parameter name in the operator position of `(op (car L) ...)` on line 5. Passing `*` or `+` changes the operation without changing the recursion.

steps.question: When `(oplist * (list 2 4 6))` runs on line 7, what expression does line 5 build before the base case `(car '(6))` returns `6`, and what number does it print?
steps.answer: It builds `(* 2 (* 4 6))`, where the base case returns `6`. The inner multiplication returns its product, and the outer multiplication prints `48`.

steps.description: Lines 7-9 display `(oplist * (list 2 4 6))` and `(apply * (list 2 4 6))`, printing `48` on both lines.
